options: An external system creates or updates records inside Fusion
An external system reads data out of Fusion
A Fusion user logging into the UI
Deleting all integration users
questions.explain: Inbound means data is being written into Fusion from an external system.

questions.q: A data warehouse calls GET /journals nightly to pull GL entries. What direction is this?
options: Inbound
Outbound
Neither — GET requests have no direction
Event-driven only
questions.explain: Reading Fusion data out to an external system is an outbound integration.

questions.q: Is integration direction (inbound/outbound) the same decision as integration pattern (batch/real-time/event-driven)?
options: Yes, they are the same thing
Direction only applies to batch integrations
No — they are independent decisions; any pattern can run inbound or outbound
Pattern only applies to inbound integrations
questions.explain: Direction and pattern are separate, independent dimensions of an integration.

questions.q: Which is a classic example of an inbound Financials integration?
options: A BI tool extracting AP aging data for a dashboard
A user viewing a report in Fusion's UI
A tax engine reading invoice tax lines
A bank statement feed creating cash transactions in Cash Management
questions.explain: A bank feed creating transactions in Fusion is writing data in — inbound.

questions.q: As a rule of thumb, which HTTP verb typically signals an inbound integration against Fusion's REST API?
options: GET
OPTIONS
HEAD
POST or PATCH
questions.explain: POST/PATCH write data into Fusion, typically signaling inbound integration.
